findings: fetchLivePrice calls pricingApi.get with no timeout configured (explicitly noted in the code), so a single hung or slow call to the pricing API blocks that request indefinitely — this is the direct mechanism behind requests that time out entirely rather than merely running slow.

fetchLivePrice's catch block retries unconditionally on any error ('retry on any error'), with no maximum attempt count, no backoff, and no jitter. A permanent/non-retryable failure (invalid SKU, auth error, malformed request) causes an infinite recursive retry loop that never returns, and correlated failures across concurrent requests create a synchronized retry storm against the already-struggling pricing API, preventing it from recovering.

getDashboard awaits fetchLivePrice sequentially inside a for-loop over all of the user's orders, so total request latency scales linearly with order count (N x per-call pricing-API latency) — a serial N+1-style external-call pattern that alone explains general slowness, independent of any errors.

Because calls are serial, per-call timeout is unbounded, and failed calls retry forever, many concurrent dashboard requests under load will each hold a server request/connection slot open indefinitely waiting on the pricing API; this exhausts the shared concurrency/connection pool and can cascade into unrelated endpoints failing too, matching the reported symptom that failures occur specifically 'under load' rather than at low volume — this is the actual 'cascade' referenced in the title.

The orders query ('SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id=$1') has no LIMIT/pagination, so a user with a large order history drives a proportionally larger number of sequential external pricing calls within a single request, making both latency and the odds of hitting the hung/no-timeout path scale with account size.

The orders query uses SELECT * rather than selecting only needed columns, adding unnecessary I/O and serialization overhead on every dashboard request and coupling the endpoint to the full orders table schema.
